paragraphs.text: I am sought - that is, I am found, {a} {as Ecc 3:6} or, I am sought to by those that asked not of me - viz., by the Gentiles, who knew me not, inquired not of me. See Rom 10:20-21, where the apostle, than whom we cannot have a better interpreter, expoundeth this verse of the calling of the Gentiles, and the next verse, of the rejection of the Jews. And herein "Esaias was very bold," saith St Paul; so bold, say Origen and others, that for this cause, among others, he was sawn asunder by his unworthy countrymen. See on Isa 1:10.
paragraphs.anchor: I am sought of them that asked not for me.

paragraphs.text: The first act of our conversion then, the infusion of the sap, is of God; our will prevents it not, but follows it. See 2Co 3:5 Rom 8:7 Joh 6:44 1Co 12:3 Deu 29:3-4 Psa 36:10. Note this against the patrons of nature, freewill men, Papists especially, who not only ascribe the beginning of salvation to themselves, in co-working with God in their first conversion, but also the end and the accomplishment of it, by works of condignity, meritorious of eternal life.
paragraphs.anchor: I am found of them that sought me not.

paragraphs.text: We are not easily aroused out of that dead lethargy into which sin and Satan hath cast us; hence this "Lo I, lo I." And here we have both God’s answer to the Church’s prayer, {Isa 64:12} and the scope of the whole book, as Oecolampadius observeth, set down in the perclose - viz., the coming in of the Gentiles, and the casting off of the Jews for their many and mighty sins. {Amo 5:12}
paragraphs.anchor: I said, Behold me, behold me.

paragraphs.text: {a} Piscat.
As preachers use to do, {Pro 1:24 Act 26:1} or as those that invite and beckon others to themselves with the hand. See Mat 11:28.
paragraphs.anchor: I have spread out my hands.

paragraphs.text: Whose destruction therefore is of themselves, since they will not be ruled, reclaimed.
paragraphs.anchor: Unto a rebellious people.

paragraphs.text: Which were evil, only evil, continually so. A toad may as easily spit a cordial, as a natural man think a good thought.
paragraphs.anchor: After their own thoughts.

paragraphs.text: As it were for the nonce, in despite and defiance of me. Siquis me in faciem depalmaret, vix indignius essera laturus: I could almost as well bear a blow on the face.
paragraphs.anchor: A people that provoketh me to my face.

paragraphs.text: {a} Erected on the house tops. {2Ki 23:12 Zep 1:5} They should have offered on the golden altar only. {Exo 30:3-5}
paragraphs.anchor: And burneth incense upon altars of brick.

paragraphs.text: {a} Lateres - per meiosin cum contemptu.

Which use necromancy and consult with devils - as Saul did, and died for it - contrary to Deu 18:11. See Isa 8:19 Mar 5:5. {See Trapp on "Isa 8:19"} {See Trapp on "Mar 5:5"} This they had learned from the heathens, with whom it was common, as Tertullian teacheth.
paragraphs.anchor: Which remain among the graves.

paragraphs.text: As believing that there they should dream dreams divinatory, or have revelations in the night. By such ill arts as these, Timotheus Herulus made himself bishop of Alexandria, A.D. 467; and Boniface VIII duped Celestine V of the Popedom, A.D. 1295. Some {a} render it, that lodge with the kept ones, i.e., with their idols, which they were fain to keep, for fear they should be stolen.
paragraphs.anchor: And lodge in the monuments.

paragraphs.text: That eat swine’s flesh.] Which was flatly forbidden; {Lev 11:7} and which those martyrs in the Maccabees would rather die than do. But these belly gods, who, like swine, had their souls only to keep their bodies from putrifying, securely violated this plain law - gratifying their lusts, and making their gut their god.

They had animos in patinis, catinis, calicibus, &c. Therein they kept the broth of their swine’s flesh, {b} which they offered, and in offering eat of. But what saith one from this text? Men must not only abhor the devil’s beef, but his broth too; all occasions, appearances.
paragraphs.anchor: And broth of abominable things is in their vessels.

paragraphs.text: {a} Jun., Piscat.
{b} Porcus quasi spurcus. - Rupert.

These Jews were all manner of naughts, and therefore worthily rejected by God; necromancers, idolaters, epicures, gross hypocrites, as here their words, full of pride and contempt of others, show them to be. Such were the Pharisees with their sanctior sum quam tu {Luk 7:39} the monks and mass priests among the Papists, and the Brownists with their broad leaves of formal profession among us. From Mat 18:19, because Christ promiseth not doing for them that ask, except they agree on earth, Brownists peremptorily conclude that they ought not to pray with them that do not consent with them in their opinions; nor will they pray with their own wives and children, though never so pious, if they do not meet in the same centre of conceits. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Which say, Stand by thyself; come not near to me.

paragraphs.text: i.e., A continual offence to me, as smoke is to the nose and eyes, {Pro 10:26} and shall be perpetually tormented by me in the hottest fire of hell; whereof hypocrites are the freeholders, and other sinners are but tenants as it were to them, while they are said to have their portion with the devil and hypocrites. Some think he hinteth at their smoking and sacrificing in their gardens and groves. {Isa 65:3}
paragraphs.anchor: These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burneth all the day

paragraphs.text: {a} Abbott’s Trial of Church Forsakers, p. 148.
Heb., Before my face, as your sins were committed to my face, {Isa 65:3} which, therefore, I shall surely remember and punish.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, it is written before me.

paragraphs.text: Certo, cite, penitus, - surely, severely, suddenly; you may write upon it.
paragraphs.anchor: But will recompense, even recompense.

paragraphs.text: Your "vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers," {1Pe 1:18} whom you have striven to out sin. {Gen 15:16 Mat 23:32; Mat 23:35-36; Mat 27:25 1Th 2:15-16}
paragraphs.anchor: Your iniquities, and the iniquities of your fathers together.

paragraphs.text: Or, Reproached or dishonoured me. Displeasing service is double dishonour, because men dishonour God in that wherein they pretend (or presume at least) to please him. Such are all Popish will-worshippers; neither will it help them to plead the example of their forefathers, for here that of the prophet Ezekiel {Eze 20:18} should take place, "Walk ye not in the ways of your fathers."
paragraphs.anchor: And blasphemed me upon the hills.

paragraphs.text: Or, Lap; very largely. See Psa 79:12 Luk 6:38. I will pay them home, for the new and the old together.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore will I measure into their bosom.

paragraphs.text: This he saith in effect, I will not destroy the righteous with the wicked, but still reserve a "seed," a remnant; and this he setteth forth by a fine and fit comparison; even as the husbandman, if he find any wine in the cluster, that is, any life or sap in the vine, cutteth it not down utterly.
paragraphs.anchor: Thus saith the Lord.

paragraphs.text: So will I do for my servants’ sake.] Few though they be, even as one cluster of grapes upon a vine, yet because they are botri mustei, clusters full of new and sweet wine, full of the juice of piety, they shall be preserved.
The good husband keeps some of his corn for seed; which, though it be not much, yet it will come to much.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will bring forth a seed out of Jacob.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Reinhabit the land, a type of the last conversion of the Jews to Christ. {Rom 11:25-26}
paragraphs.anchor: And mine elect shall inherit it

paragraphs.text: The fieldlings shall be folds, and I will feed them daily and daintily {Psa 23:1} with my graces and blessings. Sharon is a very sweet and fruitful quarter, reaching from Caesarea of Palestine to Joppa; Achor is also a very rich vale near Jericho northward, {Jos 3:16} their first footing in the promised land. By both these they are assured that they shall want for nothing, and least of all for the Word of God, the food of their souls,
paragraphs.anchor: And Sharon shall be a fold of flocks.

paragraphs.text: Or, As for you, that have forsaken the Lord to observe lying vanities, and so are miserable by your own election, {Joh 12:8} you shall be yet more miserable at the great day of judgment especially, of which some take this following part of the chapter to be meant and intended. Then these improbi et reprobi shall be sure to smoke for it; then they shall return and discern between the righteous and the wicked; yea, the judge himself shall show them a manifest difference. {Isa 65:13-16}
paragraphs.anchor: But ye are they that forsake the Lord.

paragraphs.text: i.e., My temple and pure worship, which ye slight and neglect, q.d., There is no new wine in your cluster, but rather gall and deadly poison; therefore it shall be otherwise with you.
paragraphs.anchor: That forget my holy mountain

paragraphs.text: As the Israelites feasted before the Lord; {Deu 16:14-15} so in an apish imitation did the heathens before their idols; {Jdg 9:27 Eze 18:6-7 1Co 8:10} and of them these superstitious Jews had learned to do the like, in the days of Ahaz and Manasseh, who degenerated into his grandfather Ahaz, as if there had been no intervention of a Hezekiah.
paragraphs.anchor: That prepare a table for that troop.

paragraphs.text: So the prophet speaketh, as pointing to their idols, whereof they had great store. Gad (here used) and Menni (rendered number here likewise), some interpret fortune and fate; others, Jupiter and Mercury. The Septuagint, for "to that number," hath "to the devil." Oecolampadius thinks the prophet alludeth to the Pythagorean numbers, and especially to the number of four (τετρακτος), which they superstitiously observed. Others say, the Jews symbolised with the heathens in drinking to their idols by number. To such an idol they would drink so many cups, and that was called a drink offering to that number. Hence Antiphanes in Athenaeus {a} saith,
paragraphs.anchor: For that troop.

paragraphs.text: “ Adusque tria pocula venerandos esse deos. ”
{a} Lib. x.

Est elegans paronomasia: I will give you up to the sword by number and tale, to the end that none of you may escape. God usually retaliateth, and proportioneth number to number. So, choice to choice; {Isa 66:3-4} jealousy to jealousy, provocation to provocation; {Deu 32:21} device to device; {Mic 2:1; Mic 2:3} frowardness to frowardness. {Psa 18:26}
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore I will number you to the sword.

paragraphs.text: As you used to bow down to your idols.
paragraphs.anchor: And ye shall all bow down to the slaughter.

paragraphs.text: See on Pro 1:24.
paragraphs.anchor: Because when I called, ye did not answer.

paragraphs.text: Did evil things as you could; {Jer 3:5} with both hands earnestly. {Mic 7:3}
paragraphs.anchor: But did evil before mine eyes.

paragraphs.text: Lepidas antitheses ponit. You have spent your meat and drink upon idols; therefore ye shall fast another while, yea, you shall feed upon the fierce wrath of God in hell, and drink deep of that cup of his that hath eternity to the bottom.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, my servants shall eat, but ye shall be hungry.

paragraphs.text: Your hopes and hearts failing you together, ye shall pine away in your iniquities. {Eze 24:23}
paragraphs.anchor: But ye shall be ashamed.

paragraphs.text: "In the transgression of an evil man there is a snare," or a cord to strangle his joys with; "but the righteous doth sing and rejoice." {Pro 29:6} {See Trapp on "Pro 29:6"}
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, my servants shall sing.

paragraphs.text: When ye come to hell especially, where is wailing, and yelling, and gnashing of teeth.
paragraphs.anchor: And shall howl.

paragraphs.text: So that when mine elect shall denounce my curse against any one, they shall say, God make thee such another as was such a cursed wretch. See Jer 24:9; Jer 29:22; Jer 44:8; Zec 8:13, {See Trapp on "Zec 8:13"} Iadaeus sim si fallo, say the Turks at this day; As hard-hearted and unhappy as a Jew, say we.
paragraphs.anchor: And ye shall leave your name for a curse.

paragraphs.text: Jews inwardly, Israelites indeed, Christians, a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a peculiar people. {1Pe 2:9} The wicked, when they die, go out in a snuff, leave a stench behind them, as they say the devil doth when he goeth out of a room; but when the saints depart, they leave a sweet smell behind them, as those lamps do that are fed with aromatical oil. Yea, it is more than probable that in the next world we shall look upon Bradford and such with thoughts of extraordinary love and sweetness through all eternity, as Bonner and such with execration and everlasting detestation.
paragraphs.anchor: And call his servants by another name.

paragraphs.text: Or, That blesseth, either himself or any other.
paragraphs.anchor: That he who blesseth himself in the earth, &c.

paragraphs.text: Heb. Shall bless in the God of Amen - that is, say some, in Christ, who is "Amen, the faithful and true witness," {Rev 3:14} in whom all the promises are, Yea, and Amen, {2Co 1:20} and who was wont often to say, Amen, amen. Others render it thus, Benedicat sibi per Deum firmi, shall bless himself by the God of the firm or faithful people, founded and rooted in God, so as that "the gates of hell shall not prevail against them."
paragraphs.anchor: Shall bless himself in the God of truth.

paragraphs.text: Or, By the God of the firm and faithful people, as before.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall swear by the God of truth.

paragraphs.text: Remembered no otherwise than "as waters that are past." See Zec 10:6. {See Trapp on "Zec 10:6"}
paragraphs.anchor: Because the former troubles are forgotten.

paragraphs.text: I am making of a new world - that is, gospel times, called a "new creation," {2Co 5:17} and "the world to come"; {Heb 2:5} heaven beforehand. {Mat 3:2} The consummation hereof we are to expect at the last day, {2Pe 3:13 Rev 21:1; Rev 21:5} when the "former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind," because the Lord, who made heaven and earth, shall "bless his people out of Zion" {Psa 134:3}
paragraphs.anchor: For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth.

paragraphs.text: What can ye be less than everlastingly merry when you consider your gospel privileges, which are such as may well swallow up all discontents, and make you "more than conquerors," and that is triumphers?
paragraphs.anchor: But be glad and rejoice for ever.

paragraphs.text: Creo talem Ierusalem ut sit ei nomen tripudium, et populus eius vocetur gaudium. {a} Hence it appeareth that these things are not to be taken according to the letter, but of "Jerusalem which is above, that mother of us all."
paragraphs.anchor: For, behold, I create Jerusalem a rejoicing.

paragraphs.text: {a} Oecolamp.
Well may Jerusalem then rejoice in God, who as in all her afflictions he is afflicted, so he taketh pleasure in the prosperity of his people.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will rejoice in Jerusalem.

paragraphs.text: See Isa 35:10; Isa 51:12 Rev 21:4.
paragraphs.anchor: And the voice of weeping.

paragraphs.text: This verse, as some others, had been easy, had not commentators made it so knotty. There shall be no more thence - that is, from Jerusalem {Isa 65:19} - an infant of days, or a child for days; viz., that shall so die by an untimely death, for longevity is the blessing here promised.
paragraphs.anchor: There shall be no more thence an infant of days.

paragraphs.text: That hath not lived his utmost, satur dierum, as Abraham.
paragraphs.anchor: Nor an old man that hath not filled his days.

paragraphs.text: i.e., He that is now a child, shall live till he be so many years old. Note this against those that otherwise understand the words, and have therehence fished out many frivolous crotchets too long here to be related.
paragraphs.anchor: For the child shall die an hundred years old

paragraphs.text: But the sinner, being an hundred years old, {a} shall be accursed.] And the more accursed because so long lived, and yet dieth in his sin, going down to the grave with his bones full of the sins of his youth. See Ecc 8:12-13. {See Trapp on "Ecc 8:12"} {See Trapp on "Ecc 8:13"}
{a} Hinc proverb, Puer centum annorum.
The contrary whereunto is threatened against the wicked. {Deu 28:30-68} God’s people are freed from the curse of the law, from the hurt, if not from the smart of afflictions.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall build houses and inhabit them.

paragraphs.text: They shall not provide for posterity alone, but live a long while to take benefit of their own labours.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall not build, and another inhabit.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Robusti atque diuturni; they shall be hearty, healthy, and long lasting, {Psa 52:9; Psa 92:13} even as if they had eaten of that tree of life in paradise.
paragraphs.anchor: For as the days of a tree are the days of my people

paragraphs.text: As wicked men shall. {Lev 26:14-20 Deu 28:15-68 Hag 1:6; {See Trapp on "Hag 1:6"}
paragraphs.anchor: They shall not labour in vain.

paragraphs.text: Bring forth children to the murderer, {Hos 9:13} to the great grief and trouble of their poor parents.
paragraphs.anchor: Nor bring forth for trouble.

paragraphs.text: Mirabilis certe promissio, a wonderful promise, verily, saith Scultetus. The prayers of the saints do sooner pierce from their hearts to heaven, than they can find way from their hearts to their mouths. So David found it; {Psa 32:5} and Daniel; {Dan 10:12} and that prodigal. {Luk 15:18; Luk 15:20} Our Saviour, who came out of the bosom of the Father, gives two reasons (1.) "The Father himself loveth you," {Joh 16:27} and love is liberal; (2.) "The Father knoweth before ye ask, that ye have need of all these things." {Mat 6:32}
paragraphs.anchor: And it shall come to pass, that before they call I will answer.

paragraphs.text: Thus he heard those praying Israelites at the meet at Mizpeh, {1Sa 7:6} David, {Psa 6:8-9} Daniel, {Dan 9:21} Cornelius, {Act 10:3} and his company; {Act 10:44} Luther, when he came leaping out of his study, where he had been praying, with Vicimus! vicimus! in his mouth; the day is ours, we shall carry the cause.
paragraphs.anchor: And while they are yet speaking, I will hear.

paragraphs.text: Heb., As one. {a} See Isa 11:6. There shall be a holy harmony of hearts, and all good agreement among Christ’s subjects, when they come to heaven especially.
paragraphs.anchor: The wolf and the lamb shall feed together.

paragraphs.text: And dust shall be the serpent’s meat.] He shall be held in to his first condemnation. {Gen 3:14} The devil also, that old serpent, shall be limited to the heel of the saints; the head he shall not touch; he shall be tied up to his own meat - viz., that unquenchable fire prepared for him and his angels from the beginning.
See on Isa 11:9.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall not hurt, &c.

paragraphs.text: {a} Antipathiam in sympathiam convertent. - A Lapide.
